meta.title: Plugin Sorter: a free plugin manager for FL Studio on Mac
meta.description: Free, open-source plugin manager for macOS. Put a picture on every plugin in FL Studio's picker, sort VST3 and VST plugins by developer, find duplicates and remove plugins cleanly.

hero.title: The plugin manager FL Studio on Mac
hero.subtitle: Pictures for every plugin in FL Studio's picker, VST3 and VST plugins sorted by developer, and a clean way to check, turn off and remove them.
hero.note: Free, open source, Apple Silicon and Intel. macOS app, 11 or later.

picker.title: No more plugin names as plain text
picker.beforeAlt: FL Studio plugin picker where third-party plugins are plain text
picker.afterAlt: FL Studio plugin picker with a picture of every plugin, sorted into category tabs

features.title: Sort by developer
features.text: VST3 and VST plugins move into one folder per developer. You see a preview first, and one click undoes it.

features.title: Check every plugin
features.text: Find out which plugins actually load, with plain-words explanations and one-click fixes.

features.title: Clean uninstall
features.text: Remove a plugin together with its preferences, caches and installer receipts.

features.title: Find duplicates
features.text: Old versions and extra copies are listed for you. Nothing is ticked until you decide.

features.title: Turn off, don't delete
features.text: Hide a plugin from every host without removing it, and turn it back on any time.

features.title: Licenses in Keychain
features.text: Keep your plugin licenses in the macOS Keychain, with tags and colours for your own catalogue.

features.title: Cards and colour skins
features.text: Switch the list to picture cards and pick a colour skin. Working in it should feel good.

compare.title: How it differs from FL Studio's Plugin Manager
rows: One at a time by hand

install.title: Install in a minute
steps: Download PluginSorter.dmg from the latest release.
Open it and drag Plugin Sorter onto the Applications folder.
On the first launch macOS will refuse to open the app. On macOS 15 and later open System Settings, Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. On older versions right-click the app and choose Open.
install.why: The warning appears because the app is not notarized by Apple. Its source code is open on GitHub, so you can read it or build it yourself.

faq.a: Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

faq.q: Does it run on Apple Silicon?
faq.a: Yes. It is a universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later.

faq.q: Is it safe to move my plugins?
faq.a: You see every move before it happens, each run writes a log, and Undo puts everything back.

faq.q: Why does macOS warn me when I open it?
faq.a: The app is not notarized by Apple. Allow it once in System Settings, Privacy & Security, or right-click it and choose Open.
Audio Units stay in the Components folder, where macOS expects them.
